entities.summary:
Jan Stanisław Sapieha (died 1635), a prominent scion of the powerful Sapieha family, was a key figure in the political landscape of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth during the tumultuous early 17th century. As a magnate within the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, his career exemplified the intricate balance of inherited privilege, royal appointment, and personal influence that characterized the Commonwealth's unique Golden Liberty system. His ascent through significant court offices underscores the enduring power of the great Lithuanian families in shaping state policy and court intrigue during the reign of Sigismund III Vasa.

Sapieha's public service began with his appointment as starost of Słonim, a crucial administrative role, before he achieved higher courtly distinctions. In 1617, he became the Court Marshal of Lithuania, a position that placed him at the heart of the Grand Duchy's administration and royal ceremonial life, managing the monarch's household and dispensing justice within the court. His influence further solidified in 1621 when he was elevated to the prestigious office of Great Lithuanian Marshal, making him one of the highest-ranking secular officials in Lithuania, responsible for the Sejm's order, diplomatic receptions, and maintaining the dignity of the royal court. This progression of offices demonstrates his strategic political maneuvering and the trust placed in him by the monarch.

entities.summary:
Jan Stanisław Sapieha (1589–1635) was a leading magnate of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, whose career exemplified the deep entanglement of hereditary power, royal service, and regional influence that characterized the early modern Polish-Lithuanian state. Born into the immensely powerful Sapieha family, a dynasty that frequently vied for political supremacy within the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, his trajectory was shaped by both his lineage and his personal acumen in navigating the complex political landscape dominated by the Vasa kings, Sigismund III and Władysław IV. His rise through the ranks, culminating in the prestigious office of Great Lithuanian Marshal, underscores the critical role played by a handful of aristocratic families in shaping the Commonwealth's domestic and foreign policies during a period of intense geopolitical flux.

Sapieha commenced his public service as starost of Słonim, a significant administrative role, before ascending to the royal court. In 1617, he was appointed Court Marshal of Lithuania, a position that placed him in close proximity to the monarch and involved managing the royal household and court protocol. His influence further solidified when he became Great Lithuanian Marshal in 1621, a chief officer of the Grand Duchy responsible for maintaining order, presiding over the Sejm (parliament) in the absence of the king, and representing the Commonwealth abroad. During his tenure, he participated in key diplomatic missions and domestic political maneuverings that aimed to consolidate the Commonwealth's position against its eastern and northern rivals, notably Muscovy and Sweden, amidst the Thirty Years' War.
